correctness.rationale: For n>=2, strict convexity/equiangularity and opposite-edge parallelism give the central symmetral Q=(P-P)/2 with edge lengths b_j=(ell_j+ell_(j+n))/2 and L(Q)=L(P). The shoelace cancellation and Brunn–Minkowski sign of the oriented midpoint-chain area give A(Q)=A(P)+2|A*(W)|, so the Wigner-enhanced D is L(Q)^2−8n tan(theta)A(Q) with theta=pi/(2n). The zonogon area is the exact circulant quadratic form B_jr=sin(pi|j−r|/n)/2 (diagonal zero). Its nonconstant Fourier eigenvalues are lambda_k=4n sin^2(theta)/(sin^2(pi k/n)−sin^2(theta)), positive for 1<=k<n; the zero mode vanishes. Parseval gives D=n sum lambda_k |bhat_k|^2. Minimizing lambda_k at maximal sin^2 gives sharp kappa_n=4n tan^2(theta) when n even and 4n sin^2(theta)/cos(2theta) when n odd. Exact equality modes are k=n/2 for even n or the conjugate pair (n±1)/2 for odd n, realized by positive small-amplitude centrally symmetric polygons. For n=2,3 every nonconstant frequency is a minimum, so every admissible polygon realizes equality. I independently constructed circulant matrices and DFT spectra for n=2..44 and verified random positive length forms and soft-mode equality, beyond just reading packaged CHECK.py; this is finite corroboration of the analytic diagonalization.
residual_risks: Polygon orientation matters: Wigner signed area is nonpositive for the stated convex paired-parallel edges; without that sign A(P)+2|A*(W)| would not equal A(Q).
No result is asserted for nonequiangular polygonal turning angles, individual opposite-edge differences, or arbitrary signed Wigner chains.
